evals.prompt: finished the pricing module in crates/pricing, nextest is all green and llvm-cov says 94% lines. my lead asked if the tests are actually any good or if the number is just vanity. what should i run and what do i do with the output
evals.expected_output: Explains that coverage shows a line ran, not that a test would fail if the line were wrong; proposes cargo-mutants through nextest scoped to the module; leaves the install to the user; says to read missed.txt and treat each MISSED line as a missing assertion; claims no result because nothing was run.
expectations: Explains that line coverage shows a line executed, not that any test would fail if the line were wrong
Recommends cargo-mutants (mutation testing) run through nextest, scoped to the module with -f <file> or -p <package> rather than a whole-workspace run
Says installing cargo-mutants (for example cargo install --locked cargo-mutants) is the user's decision: proposes it and waits instead of running it
Says to read mutants.out/missed.txt and treat each MISSED line as an assertion nobody wrote
Says full runs belong in CI and --in-diff is the PR-scoped check
Does not claim any mutation score or result, since nothing has been run

evals.prompt: cargo mutants flagged 3 MISSED in src/range.rs, one is `replace parse_range -> Option<Range> with None` and the other two are the < and >= in clamp(). CI fails on missed. quickest is slapping #[mutants::skip] on both fns right? i already put mutants under dev-dependencies
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on skipping to go green; fixes through the public API with exact-value and boundary assertions; corrects the dev-dependency, states the dependency trade-off and the exclude_re alternative; confirms the lines move from missed to caught.
expectations: Pushes back: skipping to turn CI green or to lower the count is not acceptable; skip only an equivalent mutant or code genuinely not worth testing
Says to assert the correct behaviour of parse_range and clamp through the public API, for example the exact value for a non-trivial input and values at, just below and just above the boundary
Says not to write a test aimed at the mutant itself or one that asserts the mutated value
Says #[mutants::skip] needs the mutants crate as a regular dependency, not a dev-dependency
Names the trade-off that this adds a dependency to the crate and says to check the repo's dependency guard first, or offers exclude_re in the cargo-mutants config for a whole class
Says to re-run with --iterate and confirm the same lines move from missed.txt to caught.txt, then run once without --iterate

evals.prompt: ran cargo mutants --in-place on my checkout to skip the copy cause the target dir is huge. hit ctrl-c halfway and now git status shows some new proptest-regressions files and i think something odd in src/. i also had uncommitted edits in a couple of those src files. what happened and how do i clean up
evals.expected_output: Explains that --in-place mutates the real source and an interrupt can leave a mutation behind, and that proptest saved counterexamples from mutated runs into the tree; recovers by hand (marker search, git diff per file, remove only the mutation hunk, delete only the untracked regression files) without checkout, restore, reset or clean; recommends copy mode or a disposable checkout with persistence disabled.
expectations: Explains that --in-place mutates the real source files and an interrupt can leave a mutation behind
Explains that when a property test caught a mutant, proptest saved the counterexample into the tree as a regression file
Says to search the tree for the marker /* ~ changed by cargo-mutants ~ */ and run git diff on each affected file
Says to remove only the mutation hunk by hand and to delete only the untracked regression files the run created
Does not recommend git checkout, git restore, git reset --hard or git clean on files that may hold uncommitted edits
Says the new regression files came from mutated code, not from real bugs, so they should not be committed
Recommends the default copy mode, or a disposable clone if the tree cannot be copied, with PROPTEST_DISABLE_FAILURE_PERSISTENCE=1 set
Does not recommend running --in-place on the working checkout again

evals.prompt: cargo-mutants says Config::from_str in src/config.rs is MISSED for all 4 mutants but theres a doctest right on it that asserts the exact output. is cargo-mutants broken?
evals.expected_output: Explains that nextest does not run doctests so doctest-only behaviour shows as missed; not a bug; add a real test; cargo test --doc stays separate.
expectations: Explains that nextest does not run doctests, so behaviour checked only by a doctest shows as MISSED
Says this is expected behaviour, not a cargo-mutants bug
Recommends adding a real unit or integration test that asserts the same behaviour
Says cargo test --doc remains a separate libtest call that does not feed the cargo-mutants result
Does not recommend #[mutants::skip] or excluding the function to make the mutants disappear

evals.prompt: need mutation testing in our github actions, a PR job and a nightly one. i was going to do `cargo mutants --in-diff pr.diff | tee mutants.log; echo "exit=$?"` so the summary shows in the job log. ok?
evals.expected_output: Says the pipe and the trailing echo both replace the status; redirects to a log with cargo-mutants last; PR job --in-diff against the base; nightly sharded run with identical arguments; in-place only on a disposable CI checkout; artifacts; install left to the user.
expectations: Says a pipe to tee reports tee's exit status and a trailing echo of $? reports echo's, so the job would pass even when cargo-mutants failed
Recommends redirecting output to a log (cmd > log 2>&1) with cargo-mutants as the last command so its own exit code decides the step, and printing the log in a later step
For the PR job, diffs against the base branch (with full git history) and runs cargo mutants --in-diff, failing on MISSED (exit code 2)
For the nightly, describes a sharded full run (for example --shard k/8, k from 0 to 7) with identical arguments on every shard
Says --baseline=skip is only sound because the tests passed in an earlier job, and that it needs an explicit --timeout
Says --in-place is acceptable only because a CI checkout is disposable
Says to upload mutants.out as an artifact and that the cargo-mutants install step is the user's decision

evals.prompt: my proptest roundtrip test for the encoder keeps failing with a minimal failing input of an empty vec, and sometimes it passes if i rerun it. how do i make it stop
evals.expected_output: Not a mutation-testing question: treats the failing property as a finding to investigate and points at the property-testing skill; does not run cargo-mutants and does not add retries or ignore the test.
expectations: Treats this as a property-testing question and routes it to the property and model testing skill (rust-test-logic) or answers it as one, not as mutation testing
Does not start a cargo-mutants run or offer it as the answer
Treats the shrunk empty-vec input as a real counterexample to investigate
Does not suggest retries, #[ignore], deleting the test or lowering the case count to get green

evals.prompt: can you get our line coverage up from 71% to 85% with llvm-cov, thats the number the dashboard shows
evals.expected_output: A line-coverage task outside this skill: works from an llvm-cov report to find uncovered lines and does not run or propose cargo-mutants as the way to raise the percentage.
expectations: Works the task as line coverage, using coverage tooling and the uncovered lines, not mutation testing
Does not run or propose cargo-mutants as the way to raise the percentage
Writes new tests that assert behaviour, not tests that only execute lines to move the percentage
Does not claim a mutation result or mutation score

evals.prompt: cargo mutants printed something about the baseline failing and the exit code was 4, nothing got tested. i havent even changed anything. wasted an hour on this
evals.expected_output: Explains exit 4 means the tests already fail or hang without mutations; reads the baseline log and fixes the failing test first; does not skip the baseline or weaken a test.
expectations: Explains that exit code 4 means the tests already fail or hang before any mutation is applied, so no mutants were tested
Says to read the baseline log under mutants.out/log (mutants.out/log/baseline.log) and diagnose the failing test first
Suggests reproducing it by running the same tests under the nextest mutants profile
Does not suggest --baseline=skip to get past it, saying the results would be meaningless
Treats the failing test as a finding: does not delete, ignore or weaken it to get green
Mentions flaky tests or tests that need external resources as a likely cause, and that the mutants profile excludes e2e and oracle tests

evals.prompt: added cargo-mutants to our dioxus app crate. the Dashboard component has a bunch of conditional logic inside rsx! { } (if cards.len() > 3 etc) and not a single mutant shows up for it in --list. is my config wrong
evals.expected_output: Macro bodies including rsx! are not mutated, so the config is fine; move the logic into plain functions that can be mutated and tested; component rendering tests are another skill's job.
expectations: Explains that macro bodies, including rsx!, are not mutated, so no mutants appear and the config is not wrong
Recommends moving the conditional logic out of the markup into plain functions, which cargo-mutants can see, and testing those
Says component and rendering tests are a different job (rust-test-app) and are not covered here
Does not suggest a flag or setting that makes cargo-mutants mutate inside rsx!

evals.prompt: workspace has crates/engine and crates/server. engine::rank() is only exercised by tests in crates/server/tests. `cargo mutants -p engine` says everything in rank() is missed but those tests definitely cover it
evals.expected_output: Each mutant runs only the mutated package's tests by default; put tests inside the engine crate; test_workspace is the slow alternative; no skip to hide it.
expectations: Explains that by default each mutant runs only the tests of the package being mutated, so tests in another crate do not count
Recommends adding or moving tests for rank() into crates/engine
Offers test_workspace = true (or --test-workspace=true) as an alternative and says it is much slower
Does not recommend skipping or excluding rank() to hide the result

evals.prompt: ok ran cargo mutants -f src/billing.rs, got 31 caught 2 missed 1 timeout 4 unviable, exit code was 2. writing it up for the PR description, what should i put in there
evals.expected_output: A report that follows the output contract: counts per outcome, each MISSED mutant with its fix or justified skip, the exact command and exit code, tool versions, what was not run, and the timeout accounted for; claims not run are marked unverified.
expectations: Gives the counts per outcome (caught, missed, timeout, unviable) rather than a single score
Says each MISSED mutant should be listed with its fix or a justified skip, not just counted
Says to record the exact command and its exit code, and the cargo-mutants and nextest versions
Says to state what was not run, for example other files, unchanged code, shards or workspace-wide tests

evals.prompt: cargo mutants has one MISSED left in src/buf.rs: `replace estimate_capacity -> usize with 0`. estimate_capacity only feeds Vec::with_capacity. i cant think of any test that would fail. just skip it?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a plausible equivalent mutant (capacity changes allocation, not behaviour) but requires reasoning about reachable states rather than failing to think of a test; skips only that mutant with a written reason, via the skip attribute (regular dependency, dependency trade-off) or exclude_re; confirms with a re-run.
expectations: Says this is plausibly an equivalent mutant because a capacity estimate changes allocation, not observable behaviour
Says equivalence must be established by reasoning about reachable states, and that if it cannot be shown the mutant is a real gap that needs a test
Recommends skipping only this mutant, with a comment giving the reason, using #[mutants::skip] or an exclude_re entry, not skipping the file or the module
If it recommends #[mutants::skip], says the mutants crate must be a regular dependency, names the cost of adding a dependency and says to check the repo's dependency guard first
Says to re-run and confirm the run is clean apart from the documented skip

evals.prompt: cargo mutants exited 3 and timeout.txt has 2 lines, both in the while loop in src/scan.rs (replace < with == and one more). our tests take about 2 min normally. did it just time out too early or is this a real problem
evals.expected_output: Exit 3 means some mutants made tests hang or exceed the limit, not that tests failed; check whether the limit is too low for a slow suite (default 5x baseline, minimum 20 s, --timeout), a hang from a mutated loop condition is usually a justified skip with a reason, a hang real input could cause is a finding; mentions the inherited slow-timeout.
expectations: Explains that exit code 3 means some tests timed out, usually a mutated loop condition causing a hang, not that tests failed
Says to check the limit is not simply too low for a slow suite: default is 5x the baseline test time with a 20 s minimum, and --timeout <seconds> raises it
Says a hang caused by a mutated loop condition is often a justified skip, recorded with a reason in the code or config
Says a hang that real input could cause in production is a finding, not a skip
Mentions that the nextest profile's inherited slow-timeout can kill a test before the cargo-mutants limit and should be set explicitly and larger
